Third Part
Rights of Women Victims of Violence

Paragraph 8
Women Victims of Violence

Article 29
(1) The Regent integrates policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women into the regency development planning.
(2) The integration of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women must be incorporated into planning and budget documents which include the Regional Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPD), Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD), Strategic Plan of Regency Work Unit (Renstra-SKPK), Regency Government Work Plan (RKPK), and Work Plan and Budget of Regency Work Unit (RKA-SKPK).
(3) The Regency Work Unit whose duties and functions handle women's empowerment affairs facilitates the integration of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women into the preparation of planning documents as referred to in paragraph (2).
(4) In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (3), the work unit whose duties and functions handle women's empowerment in the region coordinates with the Regional Development Planning Agency (BAPPEDA).

Part Two
Strategy

Article 30
(1) The protection of women is implemented by integrating Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) and disaggregated data base, gender data and integrated violence data based on applicable laws and regulations.
(2) The Regency Work Unit that handles the empowerment and protection of women coordinates with other Regional Apparatus Organizations in order to realize the implementation of integrated protection of women.
(3) Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2), is carried out within the framework of strengthening synergy in policy formulation, support for programs and activities, as well as monitoring and evaluation.

Paragraph 9
Women victims of conflict

Article 12
(1) Female heads of household as referred to in Article 9 letter b, being widows whose husbands have died and as a result of divorce, must receive protection.
(2) The implementation of protection for female heads of household as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the context of providing protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, negative stigma and economic empowerment for female heads of household.
(3) Women as heads of household as referred to in paragraph (2) receive the right to protection from:
a. discriminatory actions and efforts to weaken the function of women as the economic support of the family;
b. strengthening of capacity and recognition as head of household in their environment; and
c. accessibility to economic and financial institutions.
(4) The implementation of protection for women as heads of household whose husbands have died as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. women as heads of household obtain 1/8 (one-eighth) of the total remaining assets of their husbands if she has children; and b. women as heads of household obtain 1/4 (one-quarter) of the total remaining assets of their husbands if she does not have children.
(5) The implementation of protection for women as heads of household as a result of divorce as referred to in paragraph (1) during the iddah period, the former husband is responsible for providing residence and maintenance.

Article 18
(1) The implementation of protection for women victims of violence as referred to in Article 9 letter h, in the context of providing legal protection and/or health recovery.
(2) Protection for women victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. legal assistance;
b. assistance following the occurrence of acts of violence;
c. rehabilitation and social reintegration; and
d. health services.

Article 40
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women for the following year.
(3) The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 10
The implementation of protection for women as housewives as referred to in Article 9 letter a, in the following cases: a. material and non-material support;
b. the head of the family provides special protection to the housewife during pregnancy; and
c. the housewife who has given birth must receive protection from the head of the family to reduce the burden as a housewife.

1.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text explicitly includes sexual violence within the definition of “Kekerasan”. Pasal 1 angka 11: “Kekerasan adalah setiap perbuatan ... yang berakibat timbulnya kesengsaraan atau penderitaan secara fisik, psikologis, seksual ...”. The retrieved English candidates included this exact definition (in [5.4-3]/[7.3-3], though not in the [1.2] list), but even within the [1.2] candidates the judge had access to sections about “Hak Perempuan Korban Kekerasan” and “Perempuan Korban Kekerasan” plus general violence provisions. Given the policy’s explicit inclusion of “seksual” as a form of violence, the correct label for “Sexual violence” should be Yes; the judge’s rationale was overly strict in requiring enumerated sexual-violence acts rather than recognizing the explicit inclusion of sexual suffering/violence in the definition.

5.4.evaluator_rationale: The policy includes “academics” among stakeholders with whom coordination, integration, and synergy should be improved, which implicitly covers engagement with the education sector (e.g., universities/academic institutions) in implementation/coordination.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Qanun, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bireuen Regency.
2. Regency is Bireuen Regency which is part of the provincial region of Aceh led by a Regent.
3. Regency Government is the Government of Bireuen Regency as the administration of affairs carried out by the regency government and the Regional House of Representatives of Bireuen Regency in accordance with their respective functions and authorities.
4. Regency Government is the element of Regency Government administration consisting of the Regent and regency apparatus.
5. Regent is the Head of Bireuen Regency Government who is elected through a democratic process conducted based on the principles of direct, general, free, secret, honest and fair in accordance with laws and regulations.
6. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRK is an element of the administration of Bireuen Regency government whose members are elected through general elections in accordance with laws and regulations.
7. Woman is a person (human being) who has reached the age of 15 years who menstruates, becomes pregnant, gives birth and breastfeeds.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving just and equal relations with men.
9. Victim is a woman who experiences threats of violence and or violence inside and or outside the household and or becomes an object of trafficking/exploitation, and or discrimination in all its forms and aspects.
10. Threat of Violence is any act of non-physical abuse using or not using means unlawfully that can cause danger to the body, life, freedom and human rights of women.
11. Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully, whether inside or outside the household sphere.
12. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
13. Women's Rights are all rights possessed by every woman which are part of human rights.
14. Special Protection is protection given to women and children in emergency situations, women and children in conflict with the law, women and children from minority and isolated groups, women and children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, women and children who are trafficked, women and children who are victims of abduction, sale, trafficking, women and children victims of violence both physical and/or mental.
15. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
18. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
21. Rehabilitation is a series of actions carried out by authorized parties in their field to restore the physical, mental and psychosocial condition of women to their original condition.

5.4.rationale: In the original Indonesian Pasal 3 huruf c, the policy states: “meningkatkan koordinasi ... antar SKPK dengan seluruh pemangku kepentingan baik organisasi keagamaan, organisasi profesi, akademisi, swasta dan masyarakat luas...”. “Akademisi” clearly indicates engagement with the academic/education sector as stakeholders in coordination/synergy for implementation. The judge’s Yes based on this is reasonable. Therefore the golden label “No” appears incorrect for an indicator about education institutions engagement (at least at the level of stakeholder involvement/coordination).

6.7.evaluator_rationale: While the general provisions define “Special Protection” as including women and children from minority and isolated groups, the candidate sentences do not provide any specific protection measures targeted at women from minority or isolated groups.

EXPLANATION
OF
QANUN OF BIREUEN REGENCY
NUMBER 3 YEAR 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
1. That Islamic Shari'a grants a high and noble position to women. Women have the same position as men as servants of Allah and dignified creatures. In the Al-Qur'an and the Hadith of the Prophet SAW, no teachings or activities have ever been found that lead to discrimination and exploitation of women. In fact, one of the missions of the Prophet SAW in this world is to elevate the dignity and honor of women from a very low and degrading condition.
2. That Law Number 44 Year 1999 concerning the Implementation of Special Autonomy for Aceh and Law Number 11 Year 2006 concerning the Governance of Aceh have provided a foundation for the empowerment and protection of women which is an important activity because the condition of women so far has been quite concerning in terms of education, economy, health, labor, law and even threats of violence, exploitation, discrimination, pornography and pornographic acts which are often targeted at women.
3. The obligation of the Bireuen Regency Government feels the need to have a Qanun of Bireuen Regency concerning the Empowerment and Protection of Women, it is expected that every woman can be empowered and receive protection without discrimination and also the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) which already exists in Bireuen Regency has a Juridical Foundation as one of the organizers of empowerment and protection of women in Bireuen Regency.

7.3.rationale: The golden label is No (no international donors), but the original Indonesian text does reference international assistance: Pasal 38 ayat (2) huruf f: “mengkoordinasikan peran serta dunia usaha dan kelembagaan lain, termasuk bantuan internasional bagi perlindungan perempuan”. The retrieved English candidates included this exact clause ([7.3-58]). This is sufficient to answer Yes for an indicator about international donors/assistance being contemplated as a funding/support source. Therefore the judge’s Yes is supported by the source text, and the discrepancy is best explained by the golden label being wrong rather than the model; however since the allowed root-cause set requires choosing why the discrepancy happened, this points to a golden label issue (the human-coded No conflicts with explicit ‘bantuan internasional’ language).
